title: The Gates of Jerusalem
intro: Nehemiah chapter 3 describes the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls after the exile. The gates are named with those who built them—a testimony to community and cooperation. The list proceeds counter-clockwise from the north.

items.title: Sheep Gate
items.text: Eliashib the high priest and the priests rebuilt it. It is called the Sheep Gate because sacrificial animals were brought in here to the temple.

items.title: Fish Gate
items.text: The sons of Senaah rebuilt it. Through this gate, fishermen from the coast brought their catch to the market.

items.title: Old Gate (Jeshanah Gate)
items.text: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired it. One of the oldest gates in the city.

items.title: Valley Gate
items.text: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah rebuilt it. The gate led out to the Valley of Hinnom west of the city.

items.title: Dung Gate (Refuse Gate)
items.text: Malchijah son of Recab rebuilt it. From here, garbage and waste were carried out to the Valley of Hinnom.

items.title: Fountain Gate
items.text: Shallun, the ruler of the district of Mizpah, rebuilt it. Near the Pool of Siloam and the King's Garden.

items.title: Water Gate
items.text: The temple servants living on Ophel worked here. It led down to the Gihon Spring, the city's main water source.

items.title: Horse Gate
items.text: The priests repaired this one, each in front of his own house. The king's horses were led in and out here.

items.title: East Gate (Miphkad Gate)
items.text: Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, repaired it. Also called the Muster Gate.

items.title: Guard Gate
items.text: The work was completed back at the Sheep Gate where they started—a full circle around the city.

footer.title: Spiritual Significance
footer.content: The gates represent various aspects of the Christian life: Sheep Gate (salvation through the Lamb), Fish Gate (evangelism), Water Gate (God's Word), etc. The whole people worked together—priests, goldsmiths, perfume makers, and even daughters (v.12).
